basis: Primary immunodeficiency defined by reduced numbers or impaired function of dendritic leukocytes.

decisions.haematologic: primary: deficiency or dysfunction of dendritic leukocytes is a defining blood-cell abnormality.

basis: Neuromuscular-junction disorder; pectus deformity 3/3 and spinal rigidity 2/3 support structural skeletal involvement. Ptosis and respiratory weakness reflect impaired transmission.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis in 3/3 reflects neuromuscular-junction dysfunction rather than direct eyelid or ocular tissue disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pectus deformity in 3/3 and spinal rigidity in 2/3 support substantial skeletal involvement beyond weakness.

basis: Teratoma originates in oral tissues; airway obstruction depends on tumor size. Direct airway involvement in at least 30% is not established by the supplied evidence.

decisions.pulmonary: none: the defining origin is intraoral; size-dependent airway obstruction does not establish common direct airway occupation or injury.

basis: Peroxisomal lipid disorder with defining skeletal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities; cataracts affect >80%. Respiratory involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe neurodevelopmental impairment is a defining major feature, supported by intellectual disability, CNS atrophy and delayed myelination.
decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts affect >80%; retained as the fourth axis after metabolic, skeletal and defining neurodevelopmental disease.

basis: Motor-neuron degeneration defines ALS4; muscle atrophy in 30-79% results from denervation rather than direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: common muscle wasting (30-79%) is secondary to motor-neuron loss, without evidence of intrinsic muscle injury.

basis: Retinal/CNS disease and skeletal fragility define syndrome; GI vascular bleeding ~30-50%. Marrow suppression and hepatic/portal disease omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: osteopenia with fracture susceptibility is an explicitly defining component of the syndrome.

basis: Developmental impairment and skeletal malformations define phenotype; dental defects/caries 80-99%, cardiovascular malformations 30-79%. Skin/hair variants do not establish damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the skeletal phenotype includes progressive intervertebral narrowing in 80-99% and camptodactyly in 30-79%.

basis: Endocrine, cerebral and skeletal anomalies define ECO; laryngeal/epiglottic hypoplasia 2/3 threatens airway function. Oral clefts 5/6 and eyelid fusion 4/4 omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: laryngeal and epiglottic hypoplasia in 2/3 directly compromises the airway; severity prioritizes this axis under the cap.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: cleft palate in 5/6 qualifies, but severe airway malformation takes the remaining axis.
decisions.ocular: none under cap: ankyloblepharon in 4/4 qualifies, but severe airway malformation takes priority over eyelid fusion.

basis: Spastic cerebellar/pyramidal disease; myopathic EMG in 3/6 supports muscle involvement. Bladder dysfunction 9/24 is neurogenic; cirrhosis 2/12 is below 30%.

decisions.renal: none: bladder dysfunction in 9/24 is attributable to neural dysfunction; direct urinary-organ injury is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: explicitly myopathic EMG abnormalities in 3/6 support intrinsic muscle dysfunction beyond neurologic weakness.

basis: Lymph-node lymphoid-tissue disorder; no specific infectious, autoimmune, immunodeficiency or lymphoma mechanism is established across this umbrella.

decisions.haematologic: primary: lymph nodes contain lymphoid blood-cell tissue; haematologic is the best anatomical axis for this broad disorder umbrella.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: lymph-node location alone does not establish the required mechanism; infectious lymphadenitis and lymphoma are specific subtypes.
